rationale: The named-function floor is exact 1.0: every function_definition and method_declaration is an entity, including the two that PHP hides behind an `if (! function_exists(...))` guard and the four that belong to anonymous classes (`new class implements Cache {}`), which are nameless containers holding named methods. Anonymous callables are declined an entity more often here than in other languages, and the count is a decision rather than a shortfall: all 47 in this corpus get none. 15 are callback arguments with no name at all; the other 32 are bound to a local variable, which ADR-0031's own test rejects, because a local binding is not a name a developer can refer to -- it dies when the call returns. PHP proves that rather than merely permitting it: DispatcherTestCase rebinds a single `$callback` 18, 7 and 3 times inside three data providers, so an entity per binding gave 28 distinct closure bodies just three uids between them, and same-uid entities upsert into one graph node carrying an arbitrary winner's source and the union of every edge set. That is why max_duplicate_uids is 0 rather than a tolerance. Every declined closure still has its body walked and its calls attributed to the enclosing named scope, so narrowing the rule moved neither ratio by a thousandth on either corpus -- only the Callable count, 97 to 66 here. A closure bound at module scope does keep its entity, matching the rule the TypeScript walker applies to `const foo = () => {}`; no closure in FastRoute or guzzle is bound that way, so that branch is covered by unit tests rather than by this corpus. The 4.9% call shortfall is 20 of 412 nodes and every one names its target at runtime rather than in the source: 12 dynamic instantiations (`new $this->routesConfiguration()` x6, `new $options['routeCollector']()` x5, `new $cache()` x1), 5 dynamic invocations (`$loader()` x4, `($this->routeDefinitionCallback)()` x1), and 3 `new class {}` expressions whose class has no name to point a CALLS edge at -- though those three do produce a TypeDef, an IMPLEMENTS edge and entities for their methods. Extracting any of the remaining 17 would require resolving a property, an array subscript or a local variable to a class name, which is type inference, not parsing. This selection is deliberately harder than the repo as a whole (0.951 here vs 0.968 across all 47 files) because it concentrates the dynamic-dispatch files; the fixture is the conservative measurement.
